why: THE GATHER of the repository merge train, its one statement: a train boards once min_prs pull requests would board, or once the oldest has been ready max_wait_minutes (8 ready or 5 minutes, from 23 November 2026: the owner took the improvement plan's "a lone pull request boards the train sooner" with "go with recommended options". Why: over the 30 days to 23 November the time from the last review or fix finishing to merged had a median of 1.4 hours, and a lone ready pull request always waited the full 15 minutes before a train even started. The cost: more, smaller trains, so more CI minutes per merged pull request; it is judged on the weekly scorecard's trains per day and merge latency, and the fallback is the previous value, max_wait_minutes 15, one line. min_prs stays 8. Before that: the owner's direction on 13 November 2026, "8 ready or 15 minutes, up to 40", for maximum merge speed while a lane's pull request runs no tests; it was "6 ready or 20 minutes" from 11 November). scripts/merge-train.sh reads it for its defaults (MERGE_TRAIN_MIN_PRS, MERGE_TRAIN_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES override them), and swarm-api's merge wake tick (swarm_api.trainboard) reads the same file for the deadline past which it starts one merge-train run. Here, inside swarm-api's package, because the swarm-api image installs only that package; the workflow's checkout has the whole repository.
